root_cause.text: In the F2FS `f2fs_fill_super` function, the code failed to normalize the positive return value from `f2fs_recover_fsync_data()` into a valid success code (0) when mounting read-only with recovery disabled, resulting in an invalid positive error code being passed to the VFS layer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the addition of an `else` block setting `err = 0` for read-only mounts when `err > 0`, correcting the previous behavior where the positive value was left unchanged and propagated to `vfs_get_tree()`, triggering a kernel BUG as indicated by the log "returned 1".

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement initiates the skip_recovery path that bypasses the call to f2fs_recover_fsync_data(). When recovery is skipped, the code jumps to reset_checkpoint without normalizing any potential positive return value from the recovery function to 0. This allows invalid positive error codes to propagate to the VFS layer instead of being converted to a valid success code, which is the root cause of the vulnerability.

This goto statement transfers control to reset_checkpoint without ensuring err is normalized to 0. Unlike the recovery path (lines 5219-5222) which properly normalizes positive return values to 0 for read-only mounts, this skip_recovery path allows any existing positive error value in err to propagate to the VFS layer, creating the security vulnerability.
